name: Freckle
line: Freckle places a student with a test, then adapts. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Freckle: Freckle places a student with a test, then adapts practice. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Freckle is a practice platform designed to be both student-paced and teacher-led. A student is placed by a brief assessment or a school's Star or FastBridge scores, then works an adaptive pathway and the skills or standards a teacher assigns [1][2][3]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous: every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. Freckle sets the starting point with a separate test: its own brief placement assessment, or the scores from a school's Star or FastBridge tests [1]. From there its math page says the practice continuously adapts to each student's level [3].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step and never the answer, a lesson with a worked example, a film where there is one, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. Freckle's practice is an adaptive pathway, plus the skills or standards a teacher assigns [1][3]. Its supports include hints, guided practice, instructional videos and vocabulary help [1]. A meta-analysis of 55 studies, from elementary school to college, found that worked examples improve math performance [6].

reasons.title: Who decides what comes next
reasons.body: In AMP the adult does not plan, teach or grade. AMP chooses each problem from the learner's answers. Parents and teachers see a level for each part of math and the actual problems behind every number, and each lesson has a guide for the adult. Freckle is designed to be both student-paced and teacher-led [2]. A teacher assigns skills or standards to individuals, groups or the whole class, and reads reports on usage, performance and progress [1][3].

rows.range: Kindergarten through Algebra 2 in math, aligned to state standards [1].
rows.start: A separate test: a brief placement assessment, or a school's Star or FastBridge scores [1].
rows.teaching: Hints, guided practice, instructional videos and vocabulary help, with Spanish support in many math activities [1].
rows.next: An adaptive pathway that adjusts to the student's level, plus skills or standards a teacher assigns [1][3].
rows.mastery: Mastery tracking and goal setting are described. We found no stated rule for what counts as mastered [2].

rows.print: None found in the pages we read [1][2][3].
rows.adult: A teacher assigns skills or standards to individuals, groups or the class, and reads the reports [1][3].
rows.reports: Usage, performance and progress reports, performance by standard, and class, school and district dashboards [1].
rows.evidence: Company-reported growth for students at recommended use [1]. We found no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [4][5].

theirs: Freckle is a K-12 practice platform from Renaissance, the company behind Star Assessments and FastBridge [1][2]. This page covers Freckle's math, which Renaissance lists from kindergarten through Algebra 2, aligned to state standards [1].

Freckle's home page says it is designed to be both student-paced and teacher-led [2]. A student starts with a brief placement assessment, or the school's Star or FastBridge data sets the start [1]. The student then works an adaptive pathway, and a teacher can assign skills or standards to individuals, groups or the whole class [1][3]. Supports include hints, guided practice, instructional videos and vocabulary help [1].
credit: Placement from Star or FastBridge scores, for a school that already gives those tests [1].
A teacher can aim practice at one skill or standard, for one student, a group or the class [1][3].
Spanish support in many math activities [1].

theirs: Renaissance reports that students who used Freckle at recommended levels reached median student growth percentiles of about 51 to 52 in math, against about 47 for students who did not use it [1]. It adds that consistent users, at least 18 weeks at recommended levels, gained about three extra weeks of learning [1]. The page names no sample, grades, years or study authors. Both figures compare students who met a usage target with other students, and students who use a program most can differ from the rest before they start.

Renaissance also states that a LearnPlatform study gives Freckle math ESSA Level II, moderate evidence, for grades 1 to 5 [1]. We have not reviewed that study. We found no entry for Freckle in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports, and no independent randomized trial [4][5].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. A meta-analysis of 55 studies found that worked examples improve math performance [6]. A meta-analysis of 40 studies of computer-based feedback, across ages and subjects, found the largest effects for feedback that explains [7]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and the code is public.

them: Your school already tests with Star or FastBridge and wants practice placed from those scores.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate test.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
You want AMP to choose each problem, and to see the actual problems behind every number.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Freckle?
questions.answer: Freckle places a student with a separate assessment or a school's Star or FastBridge scores, then adapts practice alongside skills a teacher assigns [1][3]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Freckle work?
questions.answer: Renaissance reports higher growth for students who used Freckle at recommended levels than for students who did not, a comparison of students who met a usage target [1]. We found no entry for Freckle in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse, and no independent randomized trial [4][5].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
